# Botbench

> Plan LEGO 51515 (Robot Inventor) and 31313 (EV3) robot builds, rehearse them in a 2D simulator, export Pybricks programs, and drive a real Inventor hub from the browser. Free, no account, nothing leaves the browser except the optional Bluetooth link.

Use this site to decide what a given pair of kits can build, to try a behaviour before flashing it, and to hand a coding agent the exact program and protocol a hub will run.

## Tabs (one page, hash routed)

- Build: https://botbench.neorgon.com/#build (kits, ports, the combination matrix and the validator)
- Simulate: https://botbench.neorgon.com/#sim (2D arena, a rule-table brain and a modes brain, a local stand-in for the Jev decider)
- Projects: https://botbench.neorgon.com/#projects (eighteen projects from first motor to two robots)
- Models and ideas: https://botbench.neorgon.com/#models (official LEGO builds, Pybricks examples, community builds, books, hardware; links only, instructions are never copied; sources checked 2026-11-03)
- Paths: https://botbench.neorgon.com/#paths (firmware paths per kit and the hardware each one needs)
- Export: https://botbench.neorgon.com/#export (Pybricks programs for InventorHub and EV3Brick, plus bridge.py for Jev)
- Link: https://botbench.neorgon.com/#link (Web Bluetooth to a Pybricks hub, or a virtual hub that is the simulator)

## Data an agent can read directly

Plain ES modules, no build step:

- Kits, ports, firmware paths and hardware extras, with source URLs: https://botbench.neorgon.com/js/catalog.js
- The project ladder: https://botbench.neorgon.com/js/projects.js
- The models catalogue and the bigger ideas: https://botbench.neorgon.com/js/models.js
- Facts, the local decider and the exact Jev request shape (TypeSafe systemone, model jev-latest): https://botbench.neorgon.com/js/brain.js
- Program generators (rulesProgram, modesProgram, bridgeScript): https://botbench.neorgon.com/js/export.js
- The hub protocol and the Web Bluetooth transport: https://botbench.neorgon.com/js/link.js

## The hub protocol

- The exported modes program prints one line twice a second: `front=…;floor=…;bumper=…;mode=…`. Sensor numbers become categories on the hub, so a language decider never sees raw numbers.
- Stdin selects a mode with one letter (f follow_line, e explore, a avoid, s stop) and drives by hand with the digits 8 2 4 6 7 9, 5 to stop.
- The link speaks the Pybricks BLE profile (service c5f50001-8280-46da-89f4-6d8051e4aeef) from Chrome or Edge over https. Firmware before Pybricks 4.0 holds one connection, so Pybricks Code must disconnect first.
- The EV3 brick has no Bluetooth LE: the Link tab and bridge.py reach the Inventor hub only. EV3 programs run on Pybricks 4.x installed over USB (since 4.0.0) or on the legacy EV3 MicroPython 2.0 image.
- Jev (TypeSafe) is called only from bridge.py on a laptop; the API key never enters the page.

## Conventions

- State lives in localStorage under `botbench-site:workbench`; the share link carries the build.
- Source, MIT: https://github.com/energon-a-secas/botbench-site
- Part of the Neorgon tool suite: https://neorgon.com/ (machine-readable index: https://neorgon.com/llms.txt)
